scope_entries.finding: Open-Meteo: keyless, one call returns current+minutely_15+hourly+daily; current.interval = 900 s and carries dew point, apparent temperature, shortwave/direct/diffuse radiation, UV, cloud cover, both pressures; no cache headers returned; minutely_15 is interpolated from hourly outside Europe/North America per its docs. MET Norway complete: keyless with mandatory User-Agent, 89-entry timeseries whose first entry is the current UTC hour, Expires about 30 min after request, Last-Modified tracks the model run, no shortwave radiation field. METAR LLBG is a keyless genuine observation roughly hourly; LLSD returns nothing (airport closed)

scope_entries.surface: measured payload sizes (om.json 39,838 B, met.json 61,934 B) x 288/day x 365
scope_entries.finding: Naive every-tick full-body storage is about 4.2 GB/yr (open-meteo, 7-day everything request) plus 6.5 GB/yr (met-no, fixed shape) on a local docker volume; met-no content is unchanged within its ~30 min Expires window, so most of that would be duplicate blobs

scope_entries.surface: IMS API PDF (ims.gov.il/sites/default/files/2023-01/API_Explanation_en.pdf, saved as scratchpad/ims_api.pdf) + keyless isr_cities.xml
scope_entries.finding: Envista API needs 'Authorization: ApiToken', granted manually by email with no stated SLA; channels include TD, RH, WS/WD/gusts, Rain, BP and measured radiation Grad/DiffR/NIP; channel ids differ per station so station metadata must be read first; PDF states observation time is always UTC+2 despite a +03:00 label; no numeric cadence or rate limit is documented; station ids for Tel Aviv Coast / Bet Dagan could not be obtained without a token. Keyless isr_cities.xml (30,922 B, ISO-8859-8) is a daily city FORECAST including 'Tel Aviv - Yafo', not observations

scope_entries.surface: OpenWeather docs via search (openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3, /price) — not fetched live, no key used
scope_entries.finding: Free 2.5 current and forecast are separate endpoints; One Call 3.0 gives 1,000 free calls/day but only with a card on file; the 60/min and 1M/month limits and the ~10 min update cadence come from issue 5 and third-party pages, not re-verified on an OpenWeather page this session; response size unmeasured

scope_entries.surface: culture-nodes/docs/adr/0001-culture-design-source.md + web/src/culture-design/README.md + org/site-astro/src/styles/global.css
scope_entries.finding: org's global.css ('First light over the mesh') is the canonical AgentCulture token contract: light/dark colour tokens verified at WCAG AA, mesh palette, Fraunces/Albert Sans type roles, motion easings and a reduced-motion kill switch. culture-nodes ADR 0001 extracts it verbatim at pinned org commit b4d939b into web/src/culture-design/ (tokens.css, mark.tsx, a 7-colour categorical palette.ts, edges.ts), never imports from the org checkout, and guards fidelity with scripts/check-culture-design.mjs. culture-nodes web is Vite + React 18 + TypeScript with @playwright/test e2e; org is Astro 7

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / recovery + data-loss lens: docker system df on this host, spec c5/h4/c7
scope_entries.finding: Spec protects the volume from the CLI's own verbs (h4) but the only copy of a year of irreplaceable observations is one named docker volume on a dev box holding 96 volumes (13 active, ~130 GB reclaimable) where pruning is likely; 'docker volume prune -a' or a manual 'volume rm' while the stack is down destroys it, and S3 is deferred. Disk capacity is not a constraint (2.2 TB free, ~10 GB/yr projected)

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / unstated-assumptions lens: scratchpad isr_cities.xml (ISO-8859-8), om.json, spec c3/c22/h2
scope_entries.finding: 'Verbatim' was never defined: inserting parsed JSON into MongoDB changes number representation and key order and cannot hold XML; the saved IMS feed is ISO-8859-8, so byte-exact storage with charset metadata is the only reading that keeps the stored-as-is decision (q1) honest

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: spec c4/c21/c29, issue 5 scheduler point 7 (jitter), MET Norway ToS
scope_entries.finding: Nothing in the spec prevents two trackers running at once (container plus a developer's host run), which would double request counts, breach met-no's Expires rule and duplicate records; overlapping ticks and per-fetch timeouts were unspecified; issue 5 asks for jitter where providers discourage synchronized calls and the spec had dropped it

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-modes lens: spec c28/h19/c33, README exit-code policy (3+ reserved)
scope_entries.finding: h19 makes staleness visible in the output, but an agent or script controlling hardware needs it machine-checkable: a stopped tracker still returns a well-formed 'latest'. Exit codes 3+ are reserved in README, so a dedicated stale code is available

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / operations + observability lens: docker info (LoggingDriver=json-file), /etc/docker/daemon.json absent
scope_entries.finding: The host's docker daemon has no log limits configured, so a tracker logging every 5 minutes for a year, or a crash-looping container, grows its log without bound; the spec had no observability beyond doctor's reachability checks

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security + privacy lens: spec c26/h17/c27/h18, MET Norway ToS 4-decimal rule
scope_entries.finding: c27 keeps the location out of the repo, but the spec did not notice that the location then leaves the machine three other ways: exact coordinates go to four third parties every 5 minutes, sit in every stored document and dump, and would be served to the network once the web service is exposed. Weather does not vary at address precision, so rounding costs nothing

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: spec c15/c16/c18/c26/c29
scope_entries.finding: Once tracker and web service moved into containers (c29), the reason for publishing mongo on host port 27020 and for a host-side pymongo extra is only the CLI's query verbs; routing them through the web API would remove both, shrinking the attack surface (no unauthenticated mongo port) at the cost of coupling the AC agent's read path to the web container. Recorded as question q2 for the user

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / lifecycle + packaging lens: pyproject.toml hatch wheel target, data-refinery-cli stack.py:46-75, .github/workflows/publish.yml
scope_entries.finding: The wheel ships only the python package; data-refinery's stack verbs locate docker-compose.yml by walking up from the module and return None from a wheel install. The spec says one CLI command brings the stack up but never said from which install. publish.yml publishes to PyPI/TestPyPI only and builds no image (TestPyPI publishing is already known to 422 for config reasons). Recorded as question q3

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / lifecycle lens (upgrade path): spec c29, version-bump-every-PR rule in tests.yml
scope_entries.finding: Every PR bumps the version, so host CLI and long-running containers drift apart routinely; nothing in the spec noticed or reported a stale image still collecting with old adapter code

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / counter-evidence lens: issue 5 acceptance criteria vs exported spec
scope_entries.finding: Checked the spec against issue 5's 16 acceptance criteria: provider capability/quota metadata, 'providers --limits', and licence/attribution documentation had no claim; Open-Meteo's free tier is CC BY 4.0 and non-commercial and MET Norway requires credit, which collides with the no-prose dashboard requirement (c30). The issue's 'current' and 'compare' verbs are covered by the latest query (c28); ecmwf/gfs are parked (v5)

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / operations lens (CI): sonar-project.properties, tests.yml lint job, decision c38
scope_entries.finding: sonar.qualitygate.wait=true with sources=climate means a build-free JS dashboard lands as uncovered new code and can turn the gate red; bandit will also flag a 0.0.0.0 bind (B104) and urllib use (B310) in the web service and adapters. No CI job can run the containers or a browser

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility + rollback lens: spec c5/h4/o6/c17
scope_entries.finding: Clean: the feature is additive (new noun groups, new compose project, new port); removing it is 'stack down' plus deleting one named volume, no sibling instance or repo is written, and agent-first verbs are untouched. Residual: reversibility of the DATA is the backup finding (c39), not this lens

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / time lens: spec h16/o12/c36, IMS PDF timestamp note, Israel DST
scope_entries.finding: Examined timestamp handling: IMS fixed-UTC+2 correction is obliged (o12) and met-no/open-meteo/METAR are UTC or carry offsets. Not previously stated and left to the plan: all stored times are UTC, the container clock is the host clock, and the dashboard alone converts to local time across DST changes

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration lens: spec c22/c37
scope_entries.finding: Clean by construction: raw fetch records are the system of record and normalized readings are re-derivable (c37), so a normalized-schema change is a re-derive, not a data migration. Holds only if the raw-record shape itself is versioned — left to the plan as a schema_version field

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / UNEXAMINED surfaces
scope_entries.finding: Not examined, and why: (1) the AC-control agent itself — it does not exist in any surveyed repo, so which variables, units and freshness it needs is unverified; (2) live IMS and OpenWeather responses — no token/key, so payload shape, size and rate behaviour rest on documentation; (3) provider terms-of-use full texts (IMS terms link, OpenWeather licence) were not read; (4) long-run behaviour of MongoDB 8 on this host under a year of append-only writes; (5) the frontend-design and dataviz skills' concrete guidance was not loaded during speccing

lapses.what: Main agent merged task t1 on its test results alone, assuming the met-no fixture was the 'complete' product the spec and the t11 brief call for; it is the 'compact' product (6 instant variables), so the met-no adapter's normalization of dew point, apparent temperature, UV, fog, cloud layers and gusts was never exercised. Found only when t11 reported the fixture lacked dew_point
lapses.skipped_check: compare each captured fixture's endpoint and variable set against the spec (s12: locationforecast/2.0/complete, 13 instant variables) before merging t1

lapses.what: Main agent merged task t12 (openweather adapter) on green tests without checking its normalized output against docs/weather-api.md section 4: the adapter emits non-vocabulary variable ids (feels_like, humidity, pressure, wind_deg) and unit ids (C, %, m/s), and its synthesized fixture is in Kelvin although the request asks for units=metric, so /latest would serve 285.32 C. Found only when the dashboard task inspected real API output
lapses.skipped_check: run each adapter's normalize() over its fixture and assert every emitted variable id and unit id is in the contract vocabulary (or x_-prefixed) before merging the adapter

lapses.what: Task agent t22, blocked by the Playwright MCP needing a system Chrome, ran 'npx playwright install chrome' which deleted the shared ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234 browser bundle before failing - a change outside its worktree on the user's machine. The main agent's brief forbade touching other repos and docker but did not forbid machine-level installs
lapses.skipped_check: brief task agents to never install or remove machine-level tooling (npx/pip/apt installs, shared caches) and to report a missing tool instead

obligations.behavior: The verbatim response body and fetch metadata are written to MongoDB before any parsing; a normalization failure leaves the raw record intact and is recorded against it
obligations.source_text: The collected weather data drives the user's home AC control — every parameter counts, so no provider field is discarded

obligations.behavior: Timeouts, non-2xx statuses, 429 and 304 each produce a stored fetch record with status and error detail; one provider failing never prevents the other providers' fetches in the same tick
obligations.source_text: climate-cli tracks Tel-Aviv-area weather every 5 minutes from several free providers, keeps every response in full (current state, forecast, all stats) in a local weather-mongodb docker instance, and the climate CLI controls the tracking service and queries what it collected

obligations.behavior: On each 5-minute tick every enabled provider is asked whether it is due per its own refresh policy; met-no is never requested before its stored Expires and sends If-Modified-Since plus the identifying User-Agent
obligations.source_text: Each provider declares its own refresh policy and the 5-minute tick honours it when deciding whether to FETCH: met-no is Expires/Last-Modified driven with conditional GET and a mandatory identifying User-Agent; open-meteo's current block is a 900-second model slice; ims and METAR follow station cadence. Every fetch that is made is stored as-is, even when its content is unchanged

obligations.seam: provider adapter -> logs and stored documents
obligations.behavior: API keys and tokens are redacted from stored request URLs, headers, log lines and error messages (openweather carries its key in the query string)
obligations.source_text: Provider API keys (IMS ApiToken, OpenWeather key) never enter the repo or the public .eidetic memory store; .gitignore already excludes .env/.envrc

obligations.behavior: Locations are read only from user configuration outside the repo; with none configured the tracker exits 2 with a remediation hint; each location multiplies per-provider request count and is refused if it would exceed a provider's configured budget
obligations.source_text: Locations are user configuration held outside the repo (never committed, including in test fixtures, docs and public eidetic memory); multiple locations are supported, bounded by each provider's request budget

obligations.behavior: up/down/status act only on this compose project; down never removes the weather-mongodb-data volume; a missing docker or compose plugin exits 2 with an install hint
obligations.source_text: Data lands in a local 'weather-mongodb' docker MongoDB instance, following the same convention used for the other services' mongodb containers on this machine

obligations.behavior: Every MongoDB access goes through one function that reads the URI from the environment and refuses host ports 27017, 27018 and 27019
obligations.source_text: The tracker never reads or writes qq-mongodb, eidetic-mongo/data-refinery-mongo, or jlab-mongodb, and this work does not touch those repos or containers (including the orphaned eidetic-mongo container)

obligations.behavior: A tracker, query or stack verb invoked without the extra installed exits 2 with the exact install command and no ImportError traceback; the agent-first verbs import no third-party module
obligations.source_text: Runtime core stays dependency-free (dependencies = []): pymongo (and any HTTP client) go in a [project.optional-dependencies] extra, lazy-imported inside command bodies; a tracker verb run without the extra exits 2 (environment error) with an install hint, never an ImportError traceback. This replaces the earlier assumption (c11) that the zero-dependency stance ends

obligations.behavior: 'latest' returns, per provider and location, every normalized value with its unit, observed_at, age and provenance (provider/source/model), in markdown by default and identically structured under --json; with no data it says so and exits 0
obligations.source_text: Output contract: markdown is the default rendering for agents and humans, --json for code; 'latest reading' is the first-class query because the AC agent controls from it

obligations.behavior: The web service opens MongoDB read-only in effect (no write routes), publishes on loopback by default, and exposes other interfaces only through an explicit configuration value
obligations.source_text: A web service, run in docker and managed by the climate CLI, serves the collected data (latest reading first) so it can be consumed from outside this machine; it includes a beautiful human-facing web app, designed with the frontend-design plugin and verified with playwright

obligations.behavior: Series are served with explicit gaps (nulls for missed ticks) and a kind tag of observation, model or forecast; the dashboard renders gaps as gaps and never interpolates across them
obligations.source_text: The web app is a graph- and chart-oriented dashboard of the data we keep, with little to no prose; charts follow the dataviz skill, the visual design follows the AgentCulture look of ../org and ../culture-nodes via the frontend-design plugin, and it is verified in a real browser with the playwright MCP

obligations.behavior: Each normalized reading stores a reference to its raw fetch record; IMS timestamps are converted from fixed UTC+2 to UTC regardless of the +03:00 label; units are normalized to SI-style metric with the original unit retained
obligations.source_text: Storage keeps the verbatim raw provider response per fetch (body plus fetch metadata: provider, endpoint, requested_at, HTTP status, cache headers, content hash) as the system of record, with normalized 'current' readings derived from it and re-derivable; provider/source/model and observed_at vs requested_at stay distinct per issue 5

obligations.behavior: tokens.css is a verbatim copy of org's global.css at the pinned commit recorded in an ADR, verified by a check script in CI; nothing under ../org or ../culture-nodes is written
obligations.source_text: The dashboard carries the AgentCulture design system by point-in-time extraction, the way culture-nodes does: org's site-astro/src/styles/global.css tokens copied verbatim at a pinned org commit into this repo with an ADR recording the pin; ../org and ../culture-nodes are read-only sources and are never modified or imported at build or run time

obligations.behavior: No test opens a network socket to a provider or to MongoDB; provider behaviour comes from captured fixtures for a neutral location and storage from an in-memory fake
obligations.source_text: CI (tests.yml) must stay green without network, docker, or API keys: tests use captured provider fixtures and a fake/mocked Mongo layer; the lint job's gates (black, isort, flake8, bandit -r climate, markdownlint, 'teken cli doctor . --strict') and the version-check job (every PR bumps the version + CHANGELOG) all apply to this work

obligations.behavior: Host-side verbs (agent-first verbs, stack, query, providers, doctor) import only the standard library; service code inside the image, run without the extra, exits 2 with the exact install command and no ImportError traceback
obligations.source_text: Runtime core stays dependency-free (dependencies = []): the host CLI talks to the stack with docker compose and stdlib urllib only. pymongo and the web framework live in a [project.optional-dependencies] extra that the container image installs, lazy-imported inside the service code; service code run without the extra exits 2 (environment error) with an install hint, never an ImportError traceback

obligations.seam: query verb -> web service HTTP API
obligations.behavior: Query verbs call the web service over HTTP with stdlib urllib and a timeout; when the web service is unreachable they exit 2 with a remediation hint ('climate stack status'), distinct from the stale-data exit code; CLI and dashboard read the same API routes
obligations.source_text: The CLI's query verbs go through the web service's HTTP API; the host CLI never connects to MongoDB

obligations.behavior: Each provider's interval, enabled flag, request parameters and quota are read from user configuration with adapter defaults; an interval shorter than the provider's refresh policy or exceeding its quota across configured locations is rejected at startup with exit 2; changing one provider's configuration never affects another's schedule
obligations.source_text: Cadence and configuration are per provider: each provider has its own configurable poll interval, enabled flag, request parameters (e.g. forecast horizon, variables, stations) and quota, with sensible defaults in its adapter. The 5-minute tick is only the scheduler's base resolution — on each tick a provider is fetched when its own interval has elapsed AND its refresh policy allows it: met-no is Expires/Last-Modified driven with conditional GET and a mandatory identifying User-Agent; open-meteo's current block is a 900-second model slice; ims and METAR follow station cadence. Every fetch that is made is stored as-is, even when its content is unchanged
